TYTAN Technologies

At TYTAN, we aim to set a global standard in autonomous air defense with AI-driven, cost-efficient systems that counter unmanned aerial threats at scale. We protect people. We protect critical infrastructure. We protect European sovereignty.

Now, we are looking for a new team member who is eager to make a real difference! As a Drone Technician (f/m/d), you will ensure our products are built and scaled to deliver industry-leading safety, reliability, and performance.

Your roadmap to make an impact

- Oversee and execute the hands-on manufacturing, assembly, and testing of UAVs and their subsystems
- Plan and coordinate production activities to meet project deadlines and technical requirements
- Support flight testing to validate performance, reliability, and system integration
- Develop and implement methods to improve manufacturing efficiency, quality, and traceability
- Collaborate with engineering teams to translate designs into functional prototypes and production-ready/test-ready UAVs
- Define and enhance the R&D lab setup to ensure a safe, efficient, and highly flexible environment for UAV development
- Maintain lab organization, equipment readiness, and adherence to safety standards

Job requirements

- Completed apprenticeship or craftsman training in a relevant field with 1+ years of relevant work experience
- Experience in soldering, spot welding, 3D printing.
- Working knowledge of UAV-specific electronics, avionics, and related components
- Highly self-organized, with the ability to multitask effectively in a fast-paced environment
- Entrepreneurial mindset and hands-on mentality with solid multitasking and self-organization abilities
- Excellent communication and coordination skills
- Fluent in German or English

Why TYTAN?

- Virtual stock options: Participate in our success through Virtual stock options (VSOPs) at the company's current valuation
- Monthly allowances: €106/month in flexible benefits including lunch discounts and EGYM Wellpass or shopping credit
- Regular health care events: Health check-ups, skin screenings, mental health workshops, and an annual vitamin infusion on us
- Referral bonus: Earn a reward when someone you refer joins the team
- Regular team events: On- and off-site activities to connect and celebrate together
- Corporate discounts: Exclusive employee discounts across a wide range of partner brands
- Flexibility: Flexible working hours and hybrid work model, plus a modern Munich office built for focus and collaboration
- Dynamic and fast-paced team: Be among the first to shape a deep-tech defence company redefining the future of security with an international team where your impact is immediate

About us

At TYTAN, it is more than just a job; it is about embracing autonomy, personal growth, and purpose. Make a lasting impact in the new era of defense! Join us to create a safer world for all.

WE are an equal-opportunity employer committed to fairness and inclusivity. We do not prioritize any specific religion, gender, nationality, or background. Due to security clearance requirements, affiliations with countries listed under § 13 para. 1 no. 17 SÜG may affect the application process.

Please note that we currently do not offer visa sponsorship, so we’re only able to consider candidates who already have a valid work permit. All qualified applicants are hereby encouraged to apply.

Standort: ERL S SP 9

A Snapshot of Your Day

Join our dedicated Customer Service specialists as they independently carry out maintenance and modernization measures for energy transmission networks at our international clients. You will engage in service activities involving high-voltage switchgear and components of energy transmission, both domestically and abroad, including onshore and some offshore projects. Our specialists receive qualification and certification through our in-house training center on product-related topics, as well as from external partners (e.g., TÜV). This ensures you become highly specialized while having access to extensive documentation and valuable know-how from our back office.

How You’ll Make an Impact

* Serve as the primary on-site contact for service operations at our clients’ locations, both domestically and internationally.
* Execute maintenance, inspections, fault analyses, and troubleshooting independently and systematically.
* Conduct measurements to assess the condition of components and derive necessary maintenance actions.
* Create documentation for service operations, including service reports and site logs.
* Lead your own teams as a supervisor as you gain experience.

What You Bring

* A successfully completed vocational training in electrical engineering (e.g., as a Mechatronics Technician, Industrial Electrician, or Electronics Technician).
* Initial professional experience in service activities related to energy transmission components is desirable.
* High willingness to travel (approximately 90%) for short- and medium-term assignments both domestically and internationally.
* Comfort working at heights and on scaffolding.
* Strong reliability, independence, commitment, teamwork, and a customer-oriented mindset.
* Proficient in German and good command of English, both spoken and written, along with a valid driver’s license (Class B).

About the Team

With the increasing share of renewable energy, growing energy demand, outdated infrastructure, and rising complexity, new connections are needed. Additionally, existing networks require upgrades and renewals to support the energy transition.

Who is Siemens Energy?

At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With over 100,000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world’s electricity generation.

Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation.

Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Energy: https://www.siemens-energy.com/employeevideo

Our Commitment to Diversity

Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity, we generate power. We run on inclusion, and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character—no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences.

Rewards/Benefits

In addition to an attractive remuneration package in line with the market, you can expect an attractive employer-financed company pension scheme

We also offer the opportunity to become a shareholder of Siemens Energy 

We offer a wide range of options for balancing family and career, such as flexible working time models, childcare facilities at many locations, the option of trial part-time work or a sabbatical

The professional and personal development of our employees is very important to us. We provide them with the opportunities to learn and develop in a self-determined way, various attractive programmes and learning materials are available for this purpose

We value equal opportunities and welcome applications from people with disabilities.

jobs.occupation: 3D Imaging Specialist – Collection Digitisation (m/f/d)  (Kaufmann/-frau - Digitalisierungsmanagement)
jobs.description:
**3D Imaging Specialist – Collection Digitisation (m/f/d) **

Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following two positions in the Department of Palaeontology & Historical Geology and the Department of Messel Research and Paleobiology at the Senckenberg Research Institute and Natural History Museum Frankfurt, starting as of 01 January 2027

3D Imaging Specialist – Collection Digitisation (m/f/d)

(full time / part time)

Location: Frankfurt (Hesse)

Organizational units:

Department of Palaeontology & Historlcal Geology, Section Amber Research

Department of Messel Research and Paleobiology, Section Palaeomammalogy

Department of Palaeoanthropology, Section Mammalogy

Employment scope: Full-time / Part-time

Type of contract: Project-based, fixed-term for three years

Remuneration: Collective agreement of Hesse, TV-H E 9

The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.

The city of Frankfurt, where the Senckenberg Society was originally founded, hosts the organization’s central administrative services along with two research institutes housing extensive scientific collections and one of Senckenberg’s most renowned institutions, the Senckenberg Natural History Museum Frankfurt. Senckenberg is as much a part of the city’s identity as its skyline and its traditional apple wine.

Within the framework of the project "SCRE3NED: Senckenberg Collection's RarEst – 3-dimensioNal Enhanced Digitisation", type specimens of exceptional scientific value (holotypes, paratypes and lectotypes) from various collections of the Senckenberg Research Institute and Natural History Museum Frankfurt (amber, extant and fossil mammals, Messel fossils) are digitised using micro-computed tomography (μCT), synchrotron radiation-based micro-computed tomography (SRμCT), and digital photography. The aim is to produce high-quality, standardised and FAIR-compliant 2D and 3D datasets for research, collection management and science communication.

Your tasks

- Performing and documenting μCT scans in accordance with established quality standards
- Supporting the preparation and execution of SRμCT scanning campaigns at external research facilities
- Reconstruction, segmentation and quality control of 3D image datasets
- Contributing to the implementation of photography-based digitisation methods
- Creation, maintenance and management of metadata in accordance with the FAIR principles
- Preparation and integration of digital datasets into the collection databases (DINA, SeSam/AQUiLA)
- Further development, optimisation and standardisation of workflows for the 3D digitisation of a range of different object groups
- Ensuring consistent data and file organisation as well as long-term archiving
- Collaboration with curators, scientists, IT specialists and external project partners

Your profile

- Completed vocational training in a technical or scientific field (e.g., technical assistant for natural history museums and research institutes, biological or medical laboratory technician, photographic technical assistant, preparator) or a completed university degree (Bachelor's/Master's) in biology, earth sciences, medical engineering, computer science, engineering, media technology or a related field, or a comparable qualification with relevant professional experience
- Practical experience with imaging techniques, preferably computed tomography
- Confident use of software for 3D image processing and segmentation (e.g., Avizo/Amira, VGStudio MAX, Dragonfly, 3D Slicer).
- Good IT skills and a willingness to familiarise yourself with new software environments
- Knowledge of digital data management and data organisation
- Careful and responsible handling of unique and sometimes fragile objects
- Valid category B driving licence
- A structured, independent and solution-oriented approach to work, combined with the ability to work well in a team
- Good written and spoken German and English

Desirable skills

- Experience in operating and working with computed tomography systems
- Knowledge of 3D printing techniques and of preparing models for printing
- Experience with photography-based digitisation methods, in particular photogrammetry
- Familiarity with the FAIR principles and experience with repositories for 3D data (e.g., MorphoSource) or with collection databases
- Interest in natural history collections, biodiversity research and digitisation
- Basic knowledge of vertebrate and insect morphology

We offer

- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations
- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution
- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension plan

Senckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.

How to apply?

Please submit your application electronically as a single PDF file, including a cover letter, CV, and relevant certificates and references by 04.10.2026.

If you are viewing this vacancy on an external job platform, please visit our career page (https://www.senckenberg.de/en/stellenanzeigen/ ) and apply via the corresponding "Apply" button. Applications submitted by email cannot be considered.

Contact

Senckenberg Gesellschaft für Naturforschung
Senckenberganlage 25
60325 Frankfurt am Main

For specific questions about this role, please contact Dr. Mónica M. Solórzano Kraemer monica.solorzano-kraemer@senckenberg.deandDr. Thomas Lehmann thomas.lehmann@senckenberg.de
